seoTitle: Google Sheets Tutorial for Beginners in the AI Era
metaDescription: A beginner walkthrough of Google Sheets: importing Excel files, starting from a template, conditional formatting, sharing, and what Gemini in Sheets needs before it appears.
intro:
Most Google Sheets tutorials open on a blank grid and a list of formulas to memorize. That is the part beginners find least useful. This one works from a real weekly schedule template instead, filled in with entries, given a formatting rule, and shared at the end.

It mirrors how day-to-day spreadsheet work goes: bring in data you already have, adapt a layout someone else built, and get the file in front of other people. The last step covers the AI side. Gemini in Sheets is real and useful, but it sits behind a plan requirement that most beginner guides skip over, so you should know whether you have it before you go looking for it.

steps.heading: Import an existing file
steps.body:
If your data already lives in Excel or a CSV, don't retype it. Open File > Import, upload the file, and Sheets confirms with a Success message and an Open now link. Google lists .xls, .xlsx, .xlsm, .xlt, .xltx, .xltm, .ods, .csv, .txt, .tsv and .tab as importable.

The choice that matters is Import location. There are six options: Create new spreadsheet, Insert new sheet(s), Replace spreadsheet, Replace current sheet, Append to current sheet, and Replace data at selected cell. Not every file type gets all six. With the .xlsx file in the recording, the last three are greyed out, which leaves you choosing between a new file, new tabs, or overwriting the whole spreadsheet. Replace spreadsheet deletes everything already in the open file, so pick Insert new sheet(s) unless you mean it. For plain-text files such as .csv, Sheets also asks which separator to split on, with Detect automatically as the default.

image.caption: The Import file dialog after a successful upload, with Replace current sheet and the two options below it greyed out for an .xlsx file.

steps.heading: Start from a template
steps.body:
From the Sheets home page, click Template gallery at the top right. From inside a spreadsheet, the same list is under File > New > From a template. Picking one opens your own copy, so nothing you type changes the original.

The Weekly schedule template used here has a Week of cell at the top and a grid of half-hour time slots below it. Click the date next to Week of and set your start date. The seven day headers recalculate from it, which is why the week in the recording begins on a Friday. Working inside a layout like this teaches spreadsheet structure (headers, labelled rows, merged title cells) faster than an empty grid does.

image.caption: The Weekly schedule template, with the start date set in the Week of cell and the day columns following from it.

steps.heading: Fill it in and add a conditional formatting rule
steps.body:
Type entries into the time slots (Grocery, Laundry, Shopping) and the template becomes a working document. To make certain entries stand out automatically, select the cells, then open Format > Conditional formatting. A panel titled Conditional format rules opens on the right.

Each rule has three parts: the range it applies to, a condition under Format cells if, and a formatting style. Choose Single color for a straightforward highlight, or Color scale to shade numbers from low to high. Custom formula is there for rules based on other cells, but it can only reference the same sheet without INDIRECT. When one range carries several rules, Sheets checks them top to bottom and the first true rule decides the format. Drag rules in the panel to reorder them.

image.caption: The Conditional format rules panel beside a partly filled weekly schedule, with Add another rule at the top.

steps.heading: Summarize with a few core formulas
steps.body:
Formulas turn rows into answers. SUM adds up a range, AVERAGE gives the typical value, and COUNTIF tallies cells that match a condition. For a schedule, COUNTBLANK across a day's column tells you how many slots are still free.

Always point formulas at a range such as C6:C30 instead of typing the numbers in. They recalculate the moment a cell changes. Keep dates in one format and avoid blank rows in the middle of a range, because sort and filter behave unpredictably on inconsistent data.

steps.heading: Name the file and share it
steps.body:
Click Share on a file that still says Untitled spreadsheet and Sheets stops you with a Name before sharing prompt. You can Skip, but save a real name. A collaborator's Drive fills up with untitled files fast.

In the share dialog, add people by email and choose a role for each: Viewer can only read, Commenter can read and leave comments, and Editor can change the sheet and reshare it. Under General access you can instead switch to Anyone with the link. Google caps a single share at 600 email addresses, and editing is limited to 100 open tabs or devices at once.

image.caption: The Name before sharing prompt, with the Untitled spreadsheet name still in the field and Skip and Save buttons.

steps.heading: Use Gemini in Sheets, if your plan includes it
steps.body:
The spark icon at the top right, beside Share and Upgrade, is Ask Gemini. It opens a side panel where you can ask for a table, a formula, a chart, a pivot table, conditional formatting or a written summary of the data. There is also an AI function you type straight into a cell, for example =AI("Classify this task as errand or chore", C6). It only sees the range you pass it, and it generates up to 350 cells at a time.

Both require an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. On a free personal account the panel may not appear at all. If you imported an Excel file and kept it as .xlsx, save it as a Google Sheets file first (File > Save as Google Sheets), because Gemini does not work on the .xlsx version. Google's own help pages warn that Gemini can suggest inaccurate information, so check any formula it writes against what you learned in the steps above.

costNote: Importing, templates, conditional formatting, formulas and sharing all work on a free Google account. Gemini in Sheets and the AI function do not: Google states both require an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan, and a Workspace admin can also switch them off.

troubleshooting.problem: Replace current sheet, Append and Replace data at selected cell are greyed out when importing
troubleshooting.cause: Google notes that not every file type offers all six import locations. In the recording, an .xlsx upload only allowed the first three.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Insert new sheet(s) to bring the workbook in as new tabs, then copy the rows you need into the existing sheet. If you need to append rows directly, export the data as .csv and import that.

troubleshooting.problem: No Ask Gemini button, or Gemini won't respond in this file
troubleshooting.cause: The account isn't on an eligible Workspace or Google AI plan, an admin has turned Gemini off, or the file is still an .xlsx opened in Sheets.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your plan first. If the file is still in .xlsx format, use File > Save as Google Sheets and work in the converted copy.

troubleshooting.problem: A conditional formatting rule is set up correctly but the cells don't change
troubleshooting.cause: Another rule on the same range is listed above it. Sheets applies the first rule that evaluates true and ignores the rest.
troubleshooting.fix: Open Format > Conditional formatting and drag the rule you want higher in the list.

faq.question: Which import option is safest for a beginner?
faq.answer: Insert new sheet(s). It adds the imported data as new tabs and leaves everything else alone. Replace spreadsheet overwrites the whole file.

faq.question: Does editing a template change it for everyone else?
faq.answer: No. Choosing a template from the gallery opens a copy in your own Drive.

faq.question: Is Gemini in Google Sheets free?
faq.answer: No. Google's help pages say Ask Gemini and the AI function need an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Everything else in this guide works on a free account.

faq.question: Can I let someone comment without letting them edit?
faq.answer: Yes. Give them the Commenter role in the share dialog. They can add comments but can't change any cells.
